learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of routing and how Assignments reach users
Distinguish between a Worklist (individual) and a Work Queue (team)
Select the correct routing option for a given business scenario

elements.description: Routing assigns responsibility for completing a Task to one or more users. It increases business efficiency by ensuring the most appropriate users receive the right work at the right time, orchestrating the workflow across teams.

elements.text: Routing is like assigning jobs at a shared service desk: give a named specialist individual responsibility, or put work in a shared pool for an eligible colleague. A routing rule must explicitly encode any additional selection policy.

items: WORKLIST — holds Assignments routed to a SPECIFIC user (operator) who owns the work
WORK QUEUE (work basket) — a SHARED queue for a team/Work Group; any qualified member can pull and complete the work

elements.caption: Three routing options: route to a specific user's Worklist, a shared Work Queue, or dynamically by business logic (skill, availability, or decision rule).

elements.description: Keep the Assignment with the user already working the Case — appropriate when the same person should continue.
Send the Assignment to a named operator's Worklist when one accountable individual must own the Task.
Send the Assignment to a shared Work Queue when any qualified member of a team can perform the work.
Use configured business conditions to choose a user or Work Queue. A shared destination does not by itself select the least-loaded worker or enforce a skill policy.

elements.caption: Worklist: individually routed work. Work Queue: shared work for eligible users. Conditional routing and processing permissions need explicit configuration.

elements.description: Work Groups organize shared work. Access Groups and Roles govern permissions. A Work Queue can require specified roles to process its Assignments; a Persona label alone is not a security boundary.

examPitfalls.title: Worklist vs. Work Queue
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where an assignment goes when routed to a specific operator. Candidates say 'Work Queue.' An assignment routed to a named operator goes to that operator's Worklist — a Work Queue (Workbasket) holds assignments not assigned to any specific person.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: One accountable owner → Worklist (specific user); any qualified team member → Work Queue.

examPitfalls.title: When to use business-logic routing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Business logic selects a destination using configured conditions. A fixed individual is appropriate only when that is the actual requirement.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure and test the business condition that determines the recipient; do not assume a shared queue supplies automatic load balancing.

examPitfalls.title: Route to current user
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Current user follows the runtime task context. The user who completed the preceding Assignment may differ from the original Case creator.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Same person continues → current user; otherwise pick specific user / queue / business logic.

examPitfalls.title: Routing improves efficiency
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks why Work Queues are preferred over individual routing in high-volume scenarios. Candidates say 'personal Worklists are slower.' Work Queues allow any available qualified operator to pick up work — this improves throughput and avoids bottlenecks when individuals are unavailable.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Tie routing choices to who should accountably perform the Task.

examPitfalls.title: Worklist vs. Workbasket — ownership model
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask the key difference between a Worklist and a Workbasket. Candidates say 'capacity.' A Worklist is owned by one operator; a Workbasket (Work Queue) has no single owner — any authorized operator in the associated Work Group can claim the assignment.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Worklist means individually routed work; Work Queue means shared work. Authorization is configured separately; individual routing does not guarantee that no authorized manager can inspect the work.

examPitfalls.title: Routing to a workbasket does not assign the task to anyone
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks what happens after routing to a Workbasket. Candidates say the Work Group Manager is automatically assigned. Routing to a Workbasket puts the assignment in a shared queue — no operator is assigned until one explicitly claims it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Assignment stays in the queue until eligible selection or a manager routes it to a user; the Work Group manager is not automatically the assignee.

examPitfalls.title: Routing is not authorization
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A shared queue or Persona label alone is not the complete access policy.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure the required Work Queue roles and the application’s permissions; check processing eligibility separately from routing.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A shared Claims Review Assignment must be visible to ALL 25 members of the claims team simultaneously so whichever agent is free can pick it up. A colleague suggests routing it to each agent's Worklist. What is the problem with this suggestion, and what is the correct approach?

options.text: Use one shared Work Queue Assignment that an eligible claims agent can select; a Worklist targets an individual instead of this shared pool
Place the same Assignment on every personal Worklist and rely on automatic deduplication
Route to the manager and require manual redistribution for every item
Broadcast independent copies to every Worklist and use urgency to merge the results

practiceQuiz.hint: If each agent gets their own Assignment, how many assignments are created and what conflict does that create?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Work Queue holds shared work. Individual routing targets a user; it does not automatically broadcast or duplicate an Assignment to every team member.

optionExplanations.A: The shared pool keeps this as one Assignment for eligible selection.
optionExplanations.B: Individual routing does not promise this broadcast-and-deduplicate behavior.
optionExplanations.C: Manual redistribution does not meet the requested shared-pool model.
optionExplanations.D: Independent copies are not the same as a single shared Assignment.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A new Case is created and must be routed to whoever is logged in and created it. The SA wants the assignment sent to that specific user automatically. Which routing option is correct?

options.text: Current operator — routes the assignment to the user who is currently logged in and triggered the Case creation
Work queue — routes the assignment to a shared queue for any available user to claim
Reporting manager — routes the assignment to the manager of the user who created the Case
Specific operator — routes to a hard-coded user ID entered by the SA, not the logged-in user

practiceQuiz.hint: Whoever is logged in right now = Current operator.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Current operator routes the assignment to whoever is currently logged in — the person creating the Case. Work queues are shared pools; specific operator routes to a hard-coded user.

optionExplanations.A: At this creation point the current user is the initiating user in the scenario.
optionExplanations.B: A shared destination does not target the initiating user individually.
optionExplanations.C: The manager is a different recipient from the requested creator.
optionExplanations.D: A fixed ID does not adapt to the runtime initiating user.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Contract Review' assignment must go to the manager of whichever user submitted the contract, without the SA needing to know who that person is in advance. Which routing option handles this dynamically?

options.text: Business logic routing configured to resolve the submitter’s manager and route to that user
Current user routing, which always finds a different user’s manager
A general managers’ Work Queue, which always selects the submitter’s own manager
A fixed operator ID that automatically changes for every submitter

practiceQuiz.hint: A dynamic recipient needs logic using the relevant Case/user context.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Resolve the required manager from the relevant submitter context using configured business logic. Do not assume a current-user or generic queue destination implements that relationship.

optionExplanations.A: Configured logic can resolve the relevant submitter’s manager.
optionExplanations.B: Current user does not universally mean that user’s manager.
optionExplanations.C: A general queue does not guarantee selection of this particular manager.
optionExplanations.D: A fixed ID does not change itself as submitters change.

practiceQuiz.scenario: KYC work should go to the Specialist Review Work Queue when the customer is high risk, and otherwise to the Standard Review Work Queue. How should the SA route the Step?

options.text: Business logic routing with conditions selecting the appropriate Work Queue
Specific user routing that always names the developer
Current user routing without any risk condition
No routing configuration because Pega guesses the risk policy automatically

practiceQuiz.hint: Evaluate the risk condition to choose the destination.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Conditional business logic selects the intended destination. A shared Work Queue does not automatically implement arbitrary risk or least-workload policies.

optionExplanations.A: The risk condition selects the intended queue.
optionExplanations.B: A fixed developer recipient ignores the stated risk policy.
optionExplanations.C: Keeping the current user does not evaluate the destination condition.
optionExplanations.D: The platform cannot infer an unconfigured business routing policy.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Claims Processing' step must be handled by any available claims processor rather than a specific person. The team is large and processors should self-assign from a shared pool. Which routing mechanism is correct?

options.text: A work queue — assignments are placed in a shared queue and any eligible user with access to that queue can claim and work them
Current operator — the assignment is created under the name of whoever created the Case and any processor can then impersonate that operator
Specific operator — the SA enters each processor's ID into the routing so the system cycles through them
Reporting manager — the assignment goes to the team lead who then manually delegates to individual processors

practiceQuiz.hint: Shared pool where anyone can self-assign = work queue.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A work queue is a shared assignment pool — any user with the correct access can claim and work available assignments without being directly targeted. Individual routing creates personal Worklist entries, not a shared pool.

optionExplanations.A: A shared queue fits eligible processors selecting work.
optionExplanations.B: Impersonating the creator is neither the requested model nor sound access design.
optionExplanations.C: A specific recipient is not an automatically rotating team pool.
optionExplanations.D: Manual delegation is unnecessary for the stated self-selection requirement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The Claims Work Queue should require a ClaimsProcessor access role to process its Assignments. What should the SA configure?

options.text: Required roles in the Work Queue’s Roles configuration, alongside the application’s access configuration
A Stage name containing ClaimsProcessor
A label on a Data Page without any authorization configuration
A Persona display name alone, treating it as the complete security policy

practiceQuiz.hint: Configure the queue’s role requirement rather than relying on its display name.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Required roles constrain who can process queue work. Work Groups distribute work; Personas and access configuration are related but not interchangeable security artifacts.

optionExplanations.A: Queue role requirements explicitly constrain processing eligibility.
optionExplanations.B: A Stage label does not implement access-role authorization.
optionExplanations.C: A display label is not an enforceable queue security configuration.
optionExplanations.D: A Persona name alone is not the complete access policy.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Loan Approval' Case has two steps: a credit check by an analyst and a final approval by a manager. The SA should ensure neither step is missed. Which Case design concept ensures both assignments are completed in sequence?

options.text: Two sequential Assignment Steps in one Process: credit check followed by final approval
Parallel branches that create both tasks at once
A shared queue without defining any dependency between the tasks
One Assignment with two names that automatically becomes a sequential process

practiceQuiz.hint: Sequential required steps = distinct Processes/Assignments in ordered Stage/Process steps.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Explicit sequential Steps express the dependency. Merely placing two Processes in the same Stage does not guarantee their order.

optionExplanations.A: Sequential Steps explicitly express the required dependency.
optionExplanations.B: Parallel branches permit concurrent work rather than this sequence.
optionExplanations.C: A destination queue alone does not define task dependencies.
optionExplanations.D: Listing two names does not create two sequential workflow tasks.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Document Verification should be available to eligible on-duty agents, who select the work themselves from a shared pool. Which routing option fits?

options.text: A work queue — the operations team maintains membership of the queue; whoever is on duty and claims the assignment handles it
Current user — keeps the task with the preceding user, who need not be an on-duty verifier
Specific operator — the SA enters a rotating list of user IDs in the routing rule that changes each shift
Reporting manager — escalates to a manager who then reassigns to the on-duty agent manually

practiceQuiz.hint: On-duty whoever-is-available = work queue maintained by the ops team.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A shared Work Queue supports this selection model. Configure operator associations, authorization and operational procedures separately; queue membership alone is not a shift schedule.

optionExplanations.A: The queue supplies the shared pool for eligible selection.
optionExplanations.B: Current user need not be an eligible on-duty verifier.
optionExplanations.C: Hard-coded recipients do not supply the requested shared pool.
optionExplanations.D: Manual reassignment is unnecessary when eligible users select from the queue.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA explains the difference between a worklist and a work queue to a new team member. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A worklist displays assignments routed directly to one specific user; a work queue displays assignments available for any eligible user to claim
A worklist is a shared pool for a team; a work queue is a personal to-do list for one user
A worklist displays Case history; a work queue displays pending assignments across all Case Types
A worklist and a work queue are interchangeable terms for the same Pega artifact

practiceQuiz.hint: Worklist = mine; work queue = team pool. Classic Pega distinction.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A worklist shows assignments routed specifically to the logged-in user; a work queue is a shared pool from which any eligible user can claim. They are distinct routing mechanisms, not synonyms.

optionExplanations.A: Personal routing and shared routing have different responsibility models.
optionExplanations.B: This reverses the Worklist and Work Queue definitions.
optionExplanations.C: A Worklist contains assigned work, not merely historical events.
optionExplanations.D: The two terms describe different routing destinations.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Manager Approval must be selected from a shared queue only by authorized users holding the SeniorManager access role. Which configuration fits?

options.text: Route to the appropriate Work Queue and configure SeniorManager as a required role for processing its work
Route to Current user and assume that user always has SeniorManager
Route to a manager and assume every manager inherently holds SeniorManager
Enter a wildcard role name as a fixed operator ID

practiceQuiz.hint: Role-based routing without naming individuals = work queue restricted to that Persona.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use the shared queue with the explicit required role and the appropriate application authorization. Role restrictions and recipient selection are separate concerns.

optionExplanations.A: The role requirement accompanies the shared queue destination.
optionExplanations.B: The current user is not guaranteed to have the required access role.
optionExplanations.C: A management relationship does not automatically confer an access role.
optionExplanations.D: An operator identifier is not a wildcard role selector.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The developer completes the first task during testing. The next Step is explicitly configured to route to Current user and appears on the developer’s Worklist. Why?

options.text: Current user keeps the next Assignment with the user who completed the preceding task
Work Queue routing always collapses to the developer’s personal Worklist
Manager routing always selects the original developer
Current user is an alias for a fixed developer ID stored at design time

practiceQuiz.hint: Read the configured routing option and the user who performed the preceding task.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Current user refers to the runtime task context, not a permanent Case-creator or developer assignment.

optionExplanations.A: The current-user destination follows the preceding task’s user.
optionExplanations.B: Shared-queue routing does not inherently target the developer.
optionExplanations.C: A manager destination would select a different context-dependent recipient.
optionExplanations.D: Current user is runtime context rather than a fixed design-time ID.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA asks: 'Which routing option would I use if I want the assignment always to go to the same person — the Head of Compliance, regardless of who submits or who is logged in?' What is the answer?

options.text: Specific operator — routes to a named, hard-coded user ID regardless of context
Current operator — routes to the Head of Compliance if they happen to be logged in
Work queue — places the assignment in a queue that only the Head of Compliance can access
Reporting manager — routes to the manager of whoever submitted the Case, which may or may not be the Head of Compliance

practiceQuiz.hint: Always the same fixed person = Specific operator.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Specific operator routes to a hard-coded user ID — always the same person regardless of who is logged in or who submitted. Use this only when the assignment genuinely must go to one named individual.

optionExplanations.A: A known fixed recipient fits Specific user routing.
optionExplanations.B: The current user changes with the task context.
optionExplanations.C: A shared pool is not the direct named-user destination requested.
optionExplanations.D: Different submitters may have different managers.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega System Architect is configuring routing for an Assignment Step. Which TWO routing options are available when configuring how work is distributed to users?

options.text: Route to a specific user’s Worklist
Route to a shared Work Queue
Route directly to a stylesheet as the Assignment owner
Route directly to a data-field label as the Assignment owner

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the two main routing destinations in Pega — individual and team-based.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Worklists and Work Queues are destinations for Assignments. A stylesheet or field label is not an Assignment owner.

optionExplanations.A: A user Worklist is an individual routing destination.
optionExplanations.B: A Work Queue supplies a shared destination.
optionExplanations.C: Stylesheets describe appearance, not Assignment responsibility.
optionExplanations.D: A field label does not identify an Assignment owner.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is explaining Work Queues to a new Pega developer. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Work Queues function in Pega?

options.text: Any authorized team member can pick up work from a Work Queue
Work Queues support team-based routing for shared Assignments
Work in a Work Queue is visible only to the team manager, not team members
A Work Queue requires all team members to log in with the same credentials

practiceQuiz.hint: A Work Queue is specifically designed for team visibility — recall who can access it and why.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Work Queues are shared pools where any authorized team member can view and claim Assignments — this is the core purpose of team-based routing. Each team member uses their own credentials; the queue is not manager-exclusive.

optionExplanations.A: Eligible authorized users can select from the shared pool.
optionExplanations.B: A shared queue supports team responsibility for available work.
optionExplanations.C: The shared queue is not inherently restricted to the manager alone.
optionExplanations.D: Users keep individual identities and do not need shared credentials.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer asks about individual Worklists. Which TWO statements are true about how Worklists work in Pega?

options.text: A Worklist contains Assignments routed to a specific operator
A Worklist is distinct from the shared pool of a Work Queue
Multiple users simultaneously own the same individual Assignment
Worklists are inherently unavailable to Constellation users

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish individual responsibility from the shared pool.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Worklist represents individually routed work. A shared queue has a different ownership model; neither implies legacy-only availability.

optionExplanations.A: The operator has individually routed Assignments on the Worklist.
optionExplanations.B: The shared Work Queue has a different responsibility model.
optionExplanations.C: One individually routed Assignment is not simultaneously owned by several users.
optionExplanations.D: Individual work presentation is not inherently restricted to legacy UI.

quickRecap.value: Assigns a Task to the most appropriate user(s); increases efficiency by getting the right work to the right people.
Worklist = specific user (owns it); Work Queue = shared team queue (pull-based).
Current user, specific user, Work Queue, or business logic with configured destination conditions.
Associates users and Work Queues so cross-functional teams share Assignments.

quickRecap: Worklist = personal queue (one operator). Workbasket = shared pool (any eligible team member).
